title: Hypothermia devenir prédiction after ECLS (HOPE) score
formula:
The HOPE Score is calculated based on the following inputs:

- Sex (male = 1, female = 0).
- Hypothermia with asphyxia (yes = 1, no = 0).
- Age, years.
- Potassium, mmol/L.
- CPR duration, min.
- Temperature, °C.

HOPE Score = 2.44 – 1.55*(Sex) – 1.95*(Asphyxia) – 0.0191*(Age, years) - 2.07*log~2~(Potassium, mmol/L) - 0.573*log~2~(CPR duration, min) + 0.937*(temperature, °C) - 0.0247*(temperature, °C)^2^

how_to_use.why:
- ECLS rewarming may improve survival and neurological outcomes in hypothermic cardiac arrest; however it is clinically invasive, resource-intensive, and logistically complex.
- This tool provides an expected probability of survival to hospital discharge, guiding patient selection for ECLS.
- It outperforms single-variable potassium cut-offs for determining ECLS eligibility.
- Recommended in several guidelines, including:

 - 2021 European Resuscitation Council Guidelines for[cardiac arrest in special circumstances](https://www.resuscitationjournal.com/article/S0300-9572%2821%2900064-2/fulltext?utm_source=chatgpt.com).
 - 2023 recommendations of the International Commission for Mountain Emergency Medicine for the[on-site treatment of avalanche victims](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300957223000217).
 - 2024 Wilderness Medical Society guidelines for[prevention and management of avalanche and nonavalanche snow burial accidents](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1016/j.wem.2023.05.014).
how_to_use.when:
- Apply to patients with accidental hypothermic cardiac arrest who are undergoing CPR and being considered for ECMO or cardiopulmonary-bypass rewarming.
- Ideally used before committing major resources or arranging transfer to an extracorporeal cardiac life support (ECLS)-capable center.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Derived from retrospective observational cohorts.
- Data are predominantly from adults; be cautious interpreting results in very young patients.
- Not intended for mild hypothermia without arrest, therapeutic hypothermia after normothermic arrest, or primary traumatic/medical cardiac arrest (including sepsis, endocrine crises, or major trauma).
- Witnessed arrest and cardiac activity (e.g., PEA, VF) were found to correlate with improved survival but were not included in the final score.
- Use a measured core temperature (e.g., esophageal, bladder, or epitympanic); peripheral measurements underestimate severity.
- A 10% survival-probability threshold yielded a 97% negative predictive value for futility.

next_steps.advice:
- Aucun outil de prédiction ne doit dicter la prise en charge de manière isolée ; intégrez toujours le jugement clinique et le contexte clinique.
- Consultez les recommandations locales et de spécialité pertinentes pour une prise en charge plus détaillée de l’hypothermie et de l’arrêt cardiaque hypothermique, telles que :

 - Wilderness Medicine Society.
 - International Commission for Mountain Emergency Medicine.
 - European Resuscitation Council.
 - American Heart Association.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Alerter un centre capable d'ECLS dès qu'il devient évident qu'un transfert peut être nécessaire.
- Documenter clairement la justification clinique et toutes les variables ayant guidé les décisions.
next_steps.management:
**Survival probability <10%:**

- ECLS is unlikely to confer benefit; consider withholding ECLS if no other favorable factors are present.
- Discuss goals of care with family and/or caregivers.
- Transition to conventional rewarming and prognostically-guided resuscitation measures.

**Survival probability ≥10%:**

- Notify an ECLS-capable center.
- Activate or continue ECLS rewarming protocol (may be institution-specific).
- Maintain high-quality mechanical or manual CPR, warmed IV fluids, and insulating measures while cannulation and/or transport is arranged.
